quickAnswer: In 2026, Ramazan Bayramı runs 20–22 March and Kurban Bayramı 27–30 May; in 2027, they fall on 9–11 March and 16–19 May. Most state museums open late (13:00) or close on Day 1 of Bayram, the Grand Bazaar closes Sundays and religious holidays, Topkapı Palace closes Tuesdays, and Dolmabahçe Palace closes Mondays.

body.text: Ignoring Türkiye's holiday and closure calendar can upend a well-planned week. Use these verified 2026–2027 dates and weekly museum schedules to structure your route cleanly.
Which dates are Ramazan Bayramı and Kurban Bayramı in 2026–2027?

According to the Presidency of Religious Affairs ([Diyanet 2026 Calendar](https://vakithesaplama.diyanet.gov.tr/icerik.php?icerik=153); [Diyanet 2027 Calendar](https://vakithesaplama.diyanet.gov.tr/icerik.php?icerik=154)), Ramazan Bayramı falls on 20–22 March 2026 and 9–11 March 2027, while Kurban Bayramı falls on 27–30 May 2026 and 16–19 May 2027. Each holiday begins at 13:00 on Arefe (the eve before Day 1).

body.text: Watch for 9-day bridge holidays (dokuz günlük bayram tatili): when Bayram falls midweek, administrative leave frequently stretches the break into a full nine-day domestic travel wave.
Do museums, bazaars and clinics close on national holidays?

Ministry of Culture museums usually stay open on secular holidays, but open at 13:00 on Day 1 of Ramazan and Kurban Bayramı ([The Istanbul Insider](https://theistanbulinsider.com/opening-hours-of-istanbul-sightseeing-spots-and-attractions/)). National Palaces close all day on Bayram Day 1 and 1 January, while the Grand Bazaar closes during the main religious holiday days.
Everyday services shift noticeably during public holidays:

items: Banks, post offices (PTT), and government offices: Closed on all national holidays and from 13:00 on Arefe afternoons and 28 October.

Clinics and pharmacies: Outpatient private clinics close or run reduced hours, while 24/7 hospital ERs (Acil) and rotating duty pharmacies (Nöbetçi Eczane) stay open—see our guide to [pharmacies and emergency healthcare in Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/pharmacy-healthcare-in-turkey).

Restaurants and ferries: Almost all tourist restaurants, Bosphorus ferries, and public transit run normally, often on Sunday timetables (and free municipal transit is occasionally offered in Istanbul on major holidays).

body.text: How far ahead do domestic flights and coastal hotels sell out during Bayram?

Domestic flights from Istanbul to Bodrum, Dalaman, Izmir, Antalya, and Cappadocia—plus boutique hotels along the Aegean and Mediterranean coasts—regularly sell out 8 to 12 weeks ahead of Kurban Bayramı and Ramazan Bayramı. Prices on remaining seats and sea-view rooms commonly jump 40% to 100% compared with adjacent non-holiday weeks.

Because Kurban Bayramı falls in mid-to-late May in 2026 and 2027, it overlaps prime spring travel. Book flights and coastal hotels 3–4 months ahead, or stay in Istanbul on Days 1–2 when locals head south.
Which days of the week are Topkapı, Dolmabahçe and Grand Bazaar closed?

Istanbul's three most visited historic landmarks each close on a different day of the week: Dolmabahçe Palace closes every Monday, Topkapı Palace closes every Tuesday, and the Grand Bazaar closes every Sunday ([Milli Saraylar](https://www.millisaraylar.gov.tr/Lokasyon/3/Dolmabahce-Sarayi?culture=en); [Topkapı Palace Guide](https://topkapi-palace.com/plan-your-visit-to-topkapi-palace/); [Grand Bazaar Guide](https://istanbul.com/grand-bazaar)), so order your days carefully.

items: Monday: Skip Dolmabahçe Palace, Beylerbeyi Palace, and Istanbul Archaeology Museums' closed sections; visit Topkapı Palace and the Grand Bazaar instead.
Tuesday: Skip Topkapı Palace; schedule Dolmabahçe Palace, Basilica Cistern (open daily), and Bosphorus neighbourhoods.
Sunday: Skip the Grand Bazaar; visit the Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı), which opens daily, alongside Sultanahmet mosques and museums.

body.text: Note that working mosques such as the Blue Mosque and Süleymaniye Mosque remain open daily but pause non-worshipper entry for 30–45 minutes around each of the five daily prayer times, and for roughly two hours around Friday midday prayers.

faq.q: Is Türkiye worth visiting during Ramazan (the fasting month) or Bayram?
faq.a: Yes. During Ramazan, restaurants in Istanbul, Cappadocia, and coastal towns stay open normally for visitors, and evening iftar dinners add memorable atmosphere. During Bayram itself, expect sold-out coastal resorts and festive crowds, so book early.

faq.q: Is the Spice Bazaar open on Sundays when the Grand Bazaar is closed?
faq.a: Yes. Unlike the Grand Bazaar, the Spice Bazaar in Eminönü opens seven days a week (with slightly shorter Sunday hours), closing only on the main religious holidays and 29 October.

faq.q: Are Hagia Sophia and the Basilica Cistern open on Mondays and Tuesdays?
faq.a: Yes. Both Hagia Sophia's visitor gallery and the Basilica Cistern operate seven days a week, making them reliable anchors for Monday or Tuesday Istanbul itineraries.

faq.q: Do domestic airlines add extra flights during Kurban Bayramı?
faq.a: Turkish Airlines, Pegasus, and AJet often add extra frequencies to Bodrum, Dalaman, and Antalya, yet those seats also fill quickly at top fare buckets. Book 2 to 3 months ahead rather than waiting for extra capacity.

faq.q: Does 1 May (Labour Day) affect sightseeing in Istanbul?
faq.a: Yes around Taksim Square and İstiklal Avenue, where police routinely restrict pedestrian access, metro stations (Taksim, Şişhane), and road traffic for the day. Plan Old City (Sultanahmet) or Asian-side (Kadıköy) sightseeing on 1 May instead.

faq.q: Are ATMs and credit cards affected on Turkish public holidays?
faq.a: No. Credit cards work normally everywhere and ATMs operate 24/7, though high-traffic tourist ATMs in coastal towns can run low on cash by Day 3 of a long Bayram weekend—withdraw pocket lira a day early.
